bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Prison Officer Salary Victoria

If you are looking at a **prison officer salary Victoria**, you likely have an hourly rate or a salary offer and want to see the full picture: annual pay, fortnightly take-home, tax, and super. This guide walks you through the conversion using the standard 38-hour week, the National Minimum Wage, award rates, and the latest tax and super figures.

## The Basic Formula: Hourly × Hours × 52

Annual gross pay is calculated as:

**hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For a full-time prison officer, we assume 38 hours per week (the standard full-time week under many awards and the National Employment Standards). If your role is part-time or your hours differ, adjust the weekly hours accordingly. The calculator on [the timesheet](/) lets you enter any hours per week.

### Example: $35 per hour

$35 × 38 × 52 = $69,160 per year (before tax and super).

Your fortnightly gross pay would be $69,160 ÷ 26 = $2,660. That is weekly pay ($1,330) multiplied by two.

## National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.9 per week for 38 hours. Casual employees get 25% loading, making it $33.05 per hour. However, most prison officers in Victoria are covered by an award or enterprise agreement that sets a higher minimum rate. The National Minimum Wage is the legal floor; your actual rate should be at least that.

The Fair Work Ombudsman publishes award pay guides. For prison officers, the applicable award may be the *Corrections and Detention (Private Sector) Award* or a state-based instrument. Always check your specific award or agreement.

## Victoria Full-Time Average: Not a Job Median

The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) reports that Victoria full-time ordinary time average weekly earnings were $2,041.1 in May 2026. This is an **average** across all full-time employees in Victoria, not a median for prison officers. Do not mistake it for a typical prison officer salary. Your pay may be higher or lower depending on your role, experience, and employer.

## Casual Loading and the Timesheet

If you work as a casual prison officer, you are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate. On [the timesheet](/), you enter your **base hourly rate** (the rate before loading) and tick the casual loading checkbox. The calculator automatically adds 25%. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading.

For example, if your base rate is $30 per hour, casual loading brings it to $37.50. Annual pay would be $37.50 × 38 × 52 = $74,100.

## Tax and Medicare Levy

Tax is calculated using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on the next $26,800 (up to $45,000)
- 30% on the next $90,000 (up to $135,000)
- 37% on the next $55,000 (up to $190,000)
- 45% above $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. The 2025–26 single reduction thresholds are used here because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of preparation. HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted in this estimate.

### Example Tax Calculation

For a gross annual salary of $69,160:
- Tax-free threshold: $18,200 → $0 tax
- Next $26,800 at 15% = $4,020
- Remaining $24,160 at 30% = $7,248
- Total tax = $11,268
- Medicare levy (2%) = $1,383.20
- Total deductions = $12,651.20
- Net annual pay ≈ $56,508.80
- Fortnightly net ≈ $2,173.42

## Superannuation Paid on Top

Super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid by your employer **on top** of your gross pay. It is not deducted from your hourly rate. The maximum contribution base is $270,830 per year. For a $69,160 salary, super adds $8,299.20 per year. This goes into your super fund, not your pocket.

For more details on super and salary packaging, see [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

## Using the Calculator

The [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool on this site lets you enter your hourly rate and see annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures with tax and super. Remember: the results assume the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. It is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

## Key Takeaways for Prison Officer Salary Victoria

- Annual pay = hourly rate × 38 × 52 (adjust hours if needed)
- Fortnightly pay = weekly pay × 2
- National Minimum Wage is $26.44/hour; your award likely pays more
- Casual loading is 25% on top of the base rate
- Super is 12% on top of ordinary earnings
- Victoria full-time average ($2,041.1/week) is an average, not a job median
- Tax uses 2026–27 resident rates plus 2% Medicare levy

For more reference tables, visit [reference tables](/data). For pay guides, see [pay guides](/blog).
